questions.q: You want the Diwali sale (on diwali-sale) to be part of main. What do you run?
options: git switch diwali-sale, then git merge main
git switch main, then git merge diwali-sale
git branch -d diwali-sale
git commit -m "merge"
questions.explain: You always merge INTO the branch you're on. Stand on main, then merge the feature branch in.

options: Git made a merge commit with two parents
There was a conflict
main was simply behind, so Git moved the main label forward. No new commit
Git deleted the branch
questions.explain: If main hasn't moved since the branch split, there is nothing to combine: main just catches up.

questions.q: What is special about a merge commit?
options: It has two parents: the last commit of each branch
It has no parent
It can't be seen in git log
It deletes the merged branch
questions.explain: A merge commit joins the two lines of history; git show prints both parents on its 'Merge:' line.

questions.q: When does Git stop with a merge conflict?
options: Whenever two branches changed the same file
When both branches changed the same lines differently
When a branch has more than 3 commits
When you forget --no-edit
questions.explain: Different lines (even in the same file) merge automatically. Only the same lines changed differently need a human.

questions.q: In the conflict, which version is between <<<<<<< HEAD and =======?
options: The version from the branch you are merging in (rohan-discount)
The version from the branch you are on (main)
The original version before both changes
A random version
questions.explain: HEAD = where you are now (main, Neha's ₹150). The part after ======= up to >>>>>>> rohan-discount is Rohan's ₹200.

questions.q: You edited sale.py to the agreed ₹150 and removed all markers. What's next?
options: git merge --abort
git add sale.py, then git commit
Delete the .git folder
git branch -D rohan-discount
questions.explain: git add marks the file as fixed; git commit finishes the merge with a two-parent commit. Then run python3 sale.py to test.

questions.q: (Going deeper) What is the merge base?
options: The newest commit both branches share: where they split
The first commit of the repository
The branch called main
The file with conflicts
questions.explain: Git compares base → ours and base → theirs. A line changed on only one side is taken; changed differently on both sides is a conflict.

questions.q: (Going deeper) Git merged with no conflict, but now the program crashes because Rohan renamed a function Neha still calls. What is this?
options: A fast-forward
A semantic conflict: Git can't see it, only running the code or tests can
A detached HEAD
A bug in Git
questions.explain: Git only compares lines of text. A clean merge can still be wrong code, so always run the program (and later, automatic tests) after merging.
